links.outcome: Stereotyping and clinical knowledge gaps in GPT-4 sex-tailored cardiovascular patient education content
links.effect: Qualitative analysis found female symptoms framed as deviations from a male norm, erectile dysfunction frequently omitted from male-tailored content despite explicit prompting, and gendered stereotypes (e.g., "bottling up emotions") in both versions.
links.quote: However, qualitative analysis identified instances where outputs introduced content inconsistent with an equity-oriented framework: female-tailored content occasionally framed female symptoms as deviations from a male norm, male-tailored content frequently omitted erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker despite explicit prompting, and both versions at times reflected gendered social stereotypes (e.g., "bottling up emotions") rather than clinical evidence.

unlisted_practices: Using structured prompts to instruct an LLM to add evidence-based sex-specific content to patient education materials
Assessing sex-inclusivity of patient education materials with a checklist

screen.reason: The study conducts an offline audit of GPT-4's performance in revising CVD patient education materials using structured prompting, evaluating equity, readability, and gender bias.
